title: Courgette Fritters
subtitle: Crisp shallow-fried courgette and feta fritters
excerpt: Grated courgette squeezed dry, mixed with feta, spring onion, and dill, then formed into fritters and shallow-fried until deeply golden. Serve with Greek yoghurt and lemon.

recipe.sourceNotes: Courgette fritters are adapted from the Greek kolokithokeftedes, a meze dish of grated courgette, feta, and herbs formed into patties and fried. The critical step is extracting as much water as possible from the grated courgette: courgettes are mostly water, and any excess makes the fritters steam rather than fry, leaving them soft and pale. Squeeze the grated courgette hard in a clean cloth or through a sieve with the back of a spoon.

content.text: Squeezing the water out of the courgette is the most important step: skip it and the fritters will be soft and pale instead of golden and crisp. Grate, salt, leave for 10 minutes, then wring in a clean cloth until almost no liquid comes out. The fritters should hold together when pressed but not be so dense they feel heavy.

Toss the grated courgette with half the salt in a colander. Leave for 10 minutes. Squeeze out as much liquid as possible, either in a clean cloth or by pressing through the colander with the back of a spoon.
Combine the squeezed courgette with the feta, spring onion, dill, eggs, flour, and remaining salt and pepper. Mix until the mixture holds together when pressed.

Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Scoop heaped tablespoons of the mixture into the pan. Flatten gently to 1.5 cm thick. Fry for 3 to 4 minutes per side until deep golden. Cook in batches.
Drain briefly on kitchen paper. Serve with Greek yoghurt and lemon wedges.
